features: Six radial bilaminar vanes form a three-dimensional spindle around one internal axis
Oblique primary rib units plus subordinate secondary branching relief
Tapered ends and radial gaps distinguish this from a single planar frond
Fossil-form specimen study; living posture and precise anatomy remain interpretive
rangea.claim: Original genus-level Rangea fossil-form specimen study. Six-vane radial construction is an interpretation informed by2013 published fossils; neither a scanned specimen replica nor a confident complete living organism. Preserve original uncertain affinity/scope.
rangea.observation: Personally inspected2018 Hoyal Cuthill and Han Fig1 B/J NESM F541 and D F387, explicitly separate from Stromatoveris A/C/E/G/I/K, Pteridinium F/H and Arborea L. Rangea actual fossil photos show oblique primary branches around a raised median axis and secondary/tertiary branching in J. Personally read2013 source abstract/text describing hexaradial bulb/stalk and six radial bilaminar vanes with three branching orders;2017 original accepted-manuscript indexed abstract reports microCT internal core/branch boundaries, not personally inspected scan pixels.2018 notes visible preserved petaloid counts vary with preservation. Original Monash2013 PDF and UCL landing native downloads403, web PDF screenshot cache miss, not pixel evidence.
rangea.decisions: Concept six-rayed end view is useful but whole spindle looks like a seed pod and too smoothly closed. Build six thin radial bilaminar vanes with open longitudinal recesses between, broad oblique primary ribs nested secondary relief physically integrated in vane faces, not a solid capsule or modern feather/tentacles. Modest uneven edge and fossil brown artistic palette. Lie long axis horizontally as display orientation only, no rooted living posture.

features: Two intersecting deep physical crevasses isolate tower from lower glacier
Unequal blunt shoulders and faceted ice walls
Continuous supporting glacier tile, not floating iceberg/mountain
serac.claim: Generic original geological serac form informed by modern glacier analogues, no named glacier, age, exact dimensions or hazard simulation.
serac.observation: Personally read NPS serac text and inspected actual NPS/Ryan Volum Emmons Glacier sunrise photograph. It shows angular broken serrated ice towers/ridges, steep fractured walls and irregular glacier surface, not floating ocean icebergs; separate iceberg photograph not used.
serac.decisions: Concept shows correct intersecting crevasses and raised block, but too regular cross-shaped channels and sugary fractured texture. Build irregular angular polygonal tower with tilted blunt crown, four lower surrounding ice fields and two unequal crossing channels reaching down through the tile relief. All opaque palette-only geometry, no floating blocks or hidden overlaps.

features: Real near-vertical deep opening with visible inner ice wall
Asymmetric rim with surface meltwater inlet channel
Visible nominal upper shaft section only
No black painted disk, closed bowl, invented bedrock/tunnel network
moulin-shaft.claim: Generic original moulin upper-shaft-section form, not Ryder Glacier replica or a complete underground hydrological reconstruction. Nominal scale and shallow water state artistic, no measured depth or bedrock claim.
moulin-shaft.observation: Personally inspected original NASA/John Sonntag Ryder Glacier moulin image: asymmetric elongated actual ice opening, steep scalloped pale blue inner walls, dark deep interior, surface channel entering curved rim from upper right. Personally read retained NASA field record and NASA2021 fieldwork text linking surface river to vertical shaft; Laurence Smith image not used as pixel evidence.
moulin-shaft.decisions: Concept upper shaft and inlet useful, but hero becomes a wide open front canyon and round top hole inconsistent between views. Build single coherent polygonal annulus with real steep inner wall and genuinely open lower section, no arbitrary complete bedrock tunnel. Surface channel reaches rim; water only narrow geometric ribbon following channel then inner wall, separated without coplanar overlap. Outside supporting ice block physical, no transparency.

features: Shallow rounded soil tongue projecting downslope from mantle
Broad convex downhill toe and connected upslope neck
Modest step relief legible in side/clay geometry
Uneven natural lobe outline, not regular stairs/rotational slide
solifluction-lobe.claim: Generic original solifluction-lobe geological process/form concept informed by modern analogues. No period, named site, exact dimensions, temperature or active movement asserted.
solifluction-lobe.observation: Personally read NPS Lanik/Swanson/Karpilo2019 report text via report mirror and inspected actual Fig34A, PDF p53 printed35, separately from pingos/polygons/lakes panels. A shows many low curved contour-aligned vegetated lobate steps down broad slopes. Caption distinguishes slow wet unfrozen material over frozen material from active-layer detachments, intact surface mat. Denali official text also describes soil creeping downslope.
solifluction-lobe.decisions: Concept central tongue useful but toe too tall/cliffy and repeated sharp terraces overstate shallow process. Build one dominant broad rounded tongue continuously merged into gently sloping soil mantle, maximum toe relief0.65m above neighbouring slope, secondary partial lobe subtle and offset. No separate turf slab, texture, scattered overlapping rocks or regular staircase; palette boundary subordinate to actual geometry.
